To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the neuroanatomically specific distribution of NPY Y1, NPY Y1/Y5, and NPY Y2 receptor subtypes can now be demonstrated using in vitro autoradiography.
the neuroanatomically specific distribution of NPY Y1, Y2, and Y5 receptor subpopulations can be determined by measuring GTPγ[35S] binding to NPY receptors.
NPY receptor sub-types can be functionally discriminated by agonist stimulation of guanine nucleotide binding proteins (G-proteins) in rat brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification, characterisation, localisation and functional role of neuropeptide Y (NPY) receptor subtypes in brain and periphery.
the neuroanatomcal localization of functional NPY receptor subtyes in the rat brain.
the development of novel radioligands to study the NPY receptor system in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the distribution of NPY Y1 and NPY Y2 receptor subtypes in rat forebrain, thalamus, and brain stem can be anatomically distinguished by the differential distribution of GTPγS binding in response to NPY Y1 or NPY Y2 agonist stimulation.
NPY receptor sub-types can be functionally discriminated by the use of NPY agonists to activate GTPγ[ ^{35} S ] binding in adult rat brain.
the Y1 receptor is the major receptor subtype expressed in rat brain and that the Y2/Y5 receptors are expressed in the hypothalamo-neurohypophyseal system and in the thalamus and hippocampus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the NPY Y1 subtype has a broad distribution in rat brain with a high level of expression in the frontal cortex, dentate gyrus and inferior colliculus, whereas the NPY Y2 receptor is highly expressed in the hypothalamous and substantia nigra.
the distribution of the NPY Y2 receptor subtype is similar to the distribution of the Y5 receptor in the hypothalamic nuclei, whereas the Y1 receptor has a more widespread distribution in the brain.

we have demonstrated the differential distribution of NPY receptors in adult rat brain and that this differential distribution is consistent with the distribution of the NPY peptide in rat brain and the known pharmacological properties of NPY receptor agonist and antagonist drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can show functional coupling of NPY receptor agonist stimulation of the GTPγ[35S] binding in the presence of GDP.
we have developed a novel method for the identification of NPY receptor populations.
we have developed a method for identifying the distribution of NPY receptors in brain tissue.
